source.version_note: Behavioral Sciences 16(6):932, published 5 June 2026. Supplied republished PDF carries a minor-change statement and September 2026 build metadata. Official website identifies the change as a Funding-statement correction, described by the publisher as not affecting scientific content. Prior full version not compared.
source.verification_method: All 23 supplied pages read, including complete questionnaire appendix, eight statistical tables, references and declarations. Conceptual Figure 1 and ANN Figure 2 visually inspected on pages 5 and 13. Crossref verifies title/authors/date. Selected publisher correction notice checked; original scale sources, prior full version, raw data and analysis code not independently fully read or reproduced.

citation.title: A Double-Edged Algorithm Attitude: How Appreciation and Aversion Shape Students’ AI Learning Anxiety in Higher Education

reading.source_scope_note: Cross-sectional self-report survey of 409 Chinese university students with existing weekly AI-learning use. PLS-SEM associations and same-sample ANN prediction are complementary analyses, not independent replications or identified causal pathways. Approach–avoidance conflict is an interpretation, not a separately measured process.
access_limits: All supplied pages and printed questionnaire items read. No raw questionnaire data, recruitment frame, collection dates, code, held-out external cohort or original scale article was independently obtained.
Publisher notice was checked narrowly for the reason for republication; no full version diff or independent audit of the publisher’s scientific-content statement was performed.
No author was contacted for restricted data. Cited books and sources remain secondary despite complete reading of this article.

study.sample: 450 responses online/in-person through Wenjuanxing;41 removed for short completion time/poor response quality, leaving 409. All currently enrolled Chinese university students with prior AI-learning experience and use at least weekly in the recent past.167 men/242 women;116 undergraduate/260 master/33 doctoral;91 humanities-social/157 science-engineering/161 arts. This is not a probability-representative sample and excludes nonusers/strong avoiders by design.
study.items: Nineteen adapted five-point items, translated/back-translated and reviewed by 3 experts. APE3 usefulness/effectiveness/productivity; AE3 understandability/explainability; AER2 unreliable-results/academic-integrity risk and ethical dilemmas; AAV3 reluctance/negative learning consequences; AAP4 positive evaluation of AI learning; ALA4 anxiety about learning functions/use/workings and keeping pace.
study.construct_scope: Appreciation items do not compare equal-quality AI with human advice; aversion items mix reluctance and expected educational harm. Anxiety is a self-reported learning-context state, not a clinical diagnosis. Ethical-risk items do not independently measure every privacy, bias, accountability or hallucination subdomain discussed in the introduction.
study.measurement: CR.754–.891; AE rho_A.636 and AAV.695 retained as exploratory. AE3 loading.486 and AAP3/4.640/.575 retained using aggregate CR/AVE criteria. HTMT ranges below.85, with AER/AAV.838. These checks do not establish every item’s construct meaning, unbiased translation, invariance, causal separation or absence of common-method effects.
study.PLS: APE→aversion+.101,p=.018,→appreciation+.315; AE→aversion+.114,p=.027,→appreciation+.228; AER→aversion+.592,→appreciation−.016,p=.741. Aversion/appreciation→anxiety+.576/+.156. R²aversion.409,appreciation.215,anxiety.379. Paths are adjusted self-report associations in a specified model, not intervention effects.
study.indirect: Risk→aversion→anxiety+.341,CI[.282,.399]; risk→appreciation→anxiety−.003,CI[−.019,.012],nonsignificant. Other indirect paths positive. Five-thousand bootstrap resamples quantify model uncertainty, not participants or replications. Antecedent→anxiety direct paths are absent in the displayed model; do not infer empirically established complete mediation.
study.ANN: Three two-hidden-layer sigmoid networks predict aversion, appreciation and anxiety using the same 409-person dataset with 10-fold 90/10 splits. Test RMSE means.098/.136/.121. Normalized importance ranks ethical risk highest for aversion, expectancy highest for appreciation and aversion highest for anxiety. Importance does not supply causal direction, sign, a significance test or proof that a nonsignificant linear path is absent.
study.prediction_limits: No external sample, naive/linear benchmark, full nested preprocessing/tuning details or independent software reproduction is supplied. If latent-score estimation/preprocessing used the full sample, CV would need nesting to assess the complete pipeline; actual leakage is not asserted without code. Figure 2 provides illustrative architectures, not every fitted run.
study.ambivalence: Two attitude dimensions and positive anxiety coefficients are compatible with a coexistence account. No joint individual ambivalence profile/index, approach–avoidance conflict scale, temporal conflict process or behavior/physiology demonstrates that both attitudes cause sustained tension in the same person.
study.interpretation: The authors explicitly acknowledge cross-sectional association and reciprocal possibilities, and restrict ANN to prediction. Proposed mechanisms of academic pressure, actual higher use, low control, risk salience and social comparison are not separately measured mediators. Support/training/clarity interventions remain recommendations.

summary: Add AI learning anxiety, performance expectancy, perceived explainability, perceived ethical risk and approach-avoidance conflict with separate state/perception/theoretical scope. Enrich existing aversion, appreciation and attitudinal ambivalence without equating broad positivity with a demonstrated relative preference for AI. Preserve null risk→appreciation evidence and verify the funding-only correction notice.

findings.definition: Worry, tension or unease associated with learning to understand, use or keep pace with AI tools.
findings.origin: Educational / motivational psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human affective state measured through four self-report items; no diagnosis, AI subjective emotion or causal attitude intervention established.
findings.ai_proposal: Assess voluntary self-reported difficulty and learning conditions with appropriate consent, separately from actual skill, usage, task performance and clinical anxiety. Test support with longitudinal or randomized evidence. A model’s anxious wording is not a measurement of its felt state, and no user personality should be inferred from one request.
findings.novelty_rationale: Context-specific learning anxiety differs from rejecting AI, disliking its risks, job-replacement anxiety or lack of technical competence.

evidence.quote: feelings of tension, unease, and stress
Learning how AI tools work makes me

findings.evidence_scope: The source selects/adapts learning-related items and reports associations with both attitude dimensions among weekly AI users. It does not establish severity thresholds, prevalence, temporal causes or effects in nonusers.
findings.boundary: Normal concern and transient learning discomfort are not necessarily a disorder or an irrational error. Stated anxiety, avoidance, actual harm and justified ethical concern differ. Do not suppress accurate risk information to improve a questionnaire score.

findings.definition: Believing that using a tool will improve one’s task effectiveness or productivity.
findings.origin: Educational / motivational psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Three-item expected usefulness/performance-gain judgment; actual gains and causal attitude effects not tested.
findings.ai_proposal: Compare expected task benefits with measured outcomes under realistic alternatives and costs. Separate a system’s competence from whether its use improves this user’s workflow. For agents, evaluate grounded estimates rather than confident benefit promises or unverified efficiency claims.
findings.novelty_rationale: Expected gains to one’s task differ from an agent’s abstract capability, reliability-based trust or a relative preference for algorithms.

evidence.quote: I find AI useful in my studies

findings.evidence_scope: AppendixA operationalizes expected benefit as usefulness, more effective tasks and productivity. The survey does not benchmark accuracy, efficiency or comparative human/AI performance.
findings.boundary: A capable tool may fail to help a particular task once cost, errors and integration are considered. Expectations can be warranted or mistaken; high expectancy is not automatically overconfidence, dependency or proof of productivity.

findings.definition: A person’s judgment that a system’s operation or recommendations are understandable and can be explained.
findings.origin: Educational / motivational psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Three-item perception measure; no test of objective explanation quality, faithful internal reasoning or a causal explanation intervention.
findings.ai_proposal: Measure users’ perceived understanding separately from actual comprehension, error detection, explanatory faithfulness and usable oversight. Hold content, expertise and readability constant when testing explanations. Do not report a fluent rationale as a verified causal trace.
findings.novelty_rationale: Feeling a system is understandable differs from an actual explanation method, genuine comprehension or transparent system design.

evidence.quote: I think AI algorithms are explainable

findings.evidence_scope: The adapted scale asks about general understandability/explainability and clear learning explanations. Positive links to both attitude scales are associations; actual error visibility, responsibility pressure and cognitive load are unmeasured explanatory hypotheses.
findings.boundary: Perceived clarity can coexist with misunderstanding or justified caution. A positive aversion coefficient does not justify withholding explanations. Explainability, trust, confidence and actual capability must be assessed separately.

findings.definition: Judging that using a system may create ethical problems or harm.
findings.origin: Educational / motivational psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Two-item concern/risk appraisal in this survey; not an objective audit of every AI risk or a demonstrated cause of anxiety.
findings.ai_proposal: Separate a person’s risk appraisal from substantiated privacy, fairness, reliability and accountability hazards. Elicit relevant facts and uncertainty, then evaluate safeguards and residual risk without minimizing concerns merely to promote uptake. A model can assess risk without feeling fear.
findings.novelty_rationale: An appraisal of possible ethical consequences differs from an actual violation, felt guilt, moral uncertainty about what is right, and reluctance to accept advice.

evidence.quote: concerns about potential problems arising from AI

findings.evidence_scope: The two items concern unreliable academic results/integrity and ethical dilemmas. Risk is strongly associated with aversion; its appreciation path is nonsignificant. Privacy, bias and responsibility subdomains discussed in the introduction are not separately measured.
findings.boundary: Perceived risk may be accurate or exaggerated; neither higher nor lower perceived risk is automatically better. Ethical risks need not be reducible to one score, and a nonsignificant attitude path does not prove the concerns have no consequences.

findings.definition: Simultaneous motivational pulls to pursue and avoid the same goal or object.
findings.origin: Educational / motivational psychology and human–AI interaction
findings.ai_evidence_status: Secondary motivational interpretation, not a directly measured conflict process or experimentally identified cause in this survey.
findings.ai_proposal: Where choices offer both value and risk, test competing approach and avoidance tendencies with explicit tasks, timing and justified constraints. Distinguish rational tradeoffs, incompatible instructions and uncertainty from a human felt conflict. An agent’s hesitation or balanced prose does not establish anxiety or competing subjective desires.
findings.novelty_rationale: Motivational conflict concerns opposed tendencies toward action, whereas attitudinal ambivalence concerns coexisting evaluations and can occur without felt conflict or impaired choice.

evidence.quote: drawn to AI because of its value and utility

findings.evidence_scope: Page 16 invokes Elliot’s approach–avoidance account to interpret positive and negative attitudes. No conflict scale, approach/avoidance behavior, tension mediator or longitudinal process is measured.
findings.boundary: Opposed considerations can support careful reasoning rather than dysfunction. The source does not show that every mixed attitude produces sustained tension or that resolving conflict means accepting AI. No AI subjective motive is inferred.

findings.definition: Reluctance to use or accept algorithmic judgments relative to comparable human judgment.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the original comparative concept while exposing this source’s broader educational reluctance/harm items.

evidence.quote: I feel reluctant to interact with and use

findings.evidence_scope: The source’s three-item aversion factor combines reluctance, expected worse learning and weakened ways of learning. Its+.576 anxiety path is a survey association, not a measured human-versus-AI choice effect or actual refusal behavior.
findings.boundary: Legitimate ethical concerns can motivate reluctance. Questionnaire negativity, comparative aversion and actual use differ; weekly-user sampling excludes some who avoid AI altogether.

findings.definition: Giving greater weight or preference to algorithmic than human advice in a comparable task.
findings.novelty_rationale: The paper’s named construct is operationalized as favorable AI-learning attitudes, which must not silently redefine the existing comparative entry.

evidence.quote: I appreciate the value of algorithmic
I think using AI tools to support

findings.evidence_scope: The four items measure appreciation/positivity/good idea/smart learning, with no human comparator or equal-quality advice task. The+.156 anxiety coefficient is not an estimate of the causal effect of preferring AI over humans.
findings.boundary: Absolute positive evaluation can coexist with caution and is not overreliance, endorsement of every output or evidence of a model’s liking. Preserve the construct extension and measurement limits.

findings.definition: Coexisting positive and negative evaluations of the same target within a person.
findings.novelty_rationale: The two-attitude account fits this existing concept; the organizing double-edged-attitude phrase is not a new behavior.

evidence.quote: aversion does not necessarily exclude algorithm appreciation
Algorithm appreciation and algorithm aversion can exist

findings.evidence_scope: The article discusses coexistence and models both dimensions, but supplies no individual joint ambivalence index, profile or tested interaction establishing within-person tension. Interpret as a conceptual coexistence account rather than a validated ambivalence-mediated pathway.
findings.boundary: Different people’s opposite views, two significant paths or a factor-correlation metric do not alone demonstrate simultaneous evaluations in each person. Mixed views can be warranted and need not be distressing or irrational.

source_identity_checks.location: First-page republication statement and official website Correction Statement
source_identity_checks.finding: Publisher identifies a minor correction to the Funding statement and states scientific content is unaffected. Supplied PDF funding names a Beijing municipal education-science project.
source_identity_checks.scope: Narrow publisher-notice check, not a full comparison with the original PDF, validation of funding records or independent verification that every scientific statement is unchanged.

methodological_limits: Self-reported perceived system properties are labeled stimuli in the S-O-R model but were not experimentally manipulated external exposures. Same-time association leaves reverse and reciprocal effects, unmeasured confounding and common-source measurement unresolved.

Significance, explanatory variance, fit thresholds and normalized ANN importance do not establish causal mechanisms, temporal mediation, calibrated reliance or actual learning improvement. The source itself recognizes these limits.

A greater coefficient for aversion than appreciation does not by itself prove a population-level difference without a direct coefficient contrast and measurement comparability. Their operational scales also differ.
Joint positive/negative evaluation can be reasonable. No measured conflict index or within-person longitudinal data establish that ambivalence necessarily produces anxiety.
The sample’s regular-use requirement, large master’s/arts proportions and lack of sampling frame limit transport to nonusers, other levels, countries or all students.
Risk→appreciation nonsignificance is not proof of zero association; ANN nonzero importance does not overturn a particular linear-path test or prove a new nonlinear mechanism.

The disclosed language-editing use of ChatGPT does not establish that any limitation was caused by AI. No clinical diagnosis, individual profiling or recommendation to hide risks/explanations follows.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Source preference, text usefulness and general favorable attitudes are different measures. This questionnaire’s appreciation items are positive AI-learning evaluations, not equal-content AI-versus-human preference.

As with egoism measured by a Machiavellianism instrument, inspect item wording rather than assume a familiar construct label guarantees operational equivalence. Retain the source-specific measurement boundary.
A second modeling method on the same data adds a different analysis, not causal identification or independent replication. Interpret predictions and psychological mechanisms separately.

deferred.reason: The paper’s organizing phrase overlaps existing attitudinal ambivalence and the separately defined motivational conflict concept. No additional synonym row.
Conceptual organizing framework and analysis workflow, not new psychological behaviors.
Interpretive explanations, not separately measured causal mediators here. No new mechanistic labels created from discussion alone.

limitations: One paper remains one source even with SEM, three ANN models, ten folds and 5000 bootstrap resamples. No fabricated diagnostic threshold, paper quota, annual count or ethical edge is added.
